findings.finding: The new `signer-not-on-keyring` verdict checks the signature only against the key embedded in the signature itself (`_verifies_against_own_key` builds a one-key trust root from `sshsig.embedded_public_key`). Any self-generated keypair therefore 'verifies'. Because the plan keeps the verdict out of `enforced_not_verified` for every enforced event, not only the historical class-A events, any contributor who can push to the tickets branch can author events claiming another identity's `author_id`, using a fresh key, and the enforced CI merge gate (the repo's stated real authorship control) will exit 0. The plan never says that from now on the gate no longer blocks forged authorship and only reports it. It also names no compensating control (for example, who reads the `signer-not-on-keyring` problem lines and when), and no bound such as a cutoff commit or the existing grandfathering boundary.

The planned class-B unit test sets a keyring-signed entry's signer_pubkey to null by hand, so its key is valid at its era. It never covers a key added to the keyring after the event's commit.
findings.finding: The plan says class-B entries (null signer_pubkey, key on 594c's keyring) will classify `verified` once the short-circuit is deleted. The in-session check does not test that. It only shows null-signer entries verify `certified` against their own embedded key and bind their event, which is the signer-not-on-keyring path. After the deletion these entries go through the commit-era verify and then any-key. When the commit resolves and the era check fails, they come out `key_not_valid_at_era`, which counts as enforced-not-verified and fails the run. A null signer_pubkey is evidence this can happen: compaction's `_identify_signer` → `authorship.identify_signer` searches the author's keyring as it stood at compaction time and records null only when no key there verified the signature (or the lookup failed). So these keys were probably absent from the keyring when compaction ran and added later, possibly after the events' commits. That contradicts the non-codebase AC's '0 key-not-valid-at-era'.
